The WW domains of NEDD4 family proteins most commonly recognise the PPxY (PY) motif. NEDD4 family members are involved in a number of diverse cellular processes including regulation of the trafficking, stability and signalling of membrane proteins and virus budding from infected cells.

nodes.name: Calponin/transgelin family
nodes.description: Calponin and transgelin are homologous cytoskeleton proteins that regulate actin-activated myosin motor functions in smooth muscle contraction and non-muscle cell motility during adhesion, migration, proliferation, phagocytosis, wound healing, inflammatory response and fibrotic tissue remodeling. Calponin and transgelin have each evolved into three homologous isoforms in vertebrates.

nodes.name: Calponin family
nodes.description: Calponins are cytoskeleton proteins that regulate actin-activated myosin motor functions in smooth muscle contraction and non-muscle cell motility during adhesion, migration, proliferation, phagocytosis, wound healing, inflammatory response and fibrotic tissue remodeling. Their highly conserved core structure consists of a calponin homology (CH) domain, two actin-binding motifs and three calponin-like (CLIK) repeats. The three vertebrate calponin isoforms are diverged in their C-terminal structures.

nodes.name: Transgelin family
nodes.description: Transgelins are cytoskeleton proteins that regulate actin-activated myosin motor functions in smooth muscle contraction and non-muscle cell motility during adhesion, migration, proliferation, phagocytosis, wound healing, inflammatory response and fibrotic tissue remodeling. Transgelins consist of one CH domain, one actin-binding motif and one calponin-like (CLIK) motif. Transgelins lack the C-terminal variable region found in Calponins.

nodes.name: LanC like family
nodes.description: LanCL enzymes respond to sites of protein damage arising from conversion of phosphorylated Ser and Thr residues into highly reactive non-canonical amino acids, catalyzing irreversible capping of the residues with glutathione.

nodes.name: Transition proteins
nodes.description: The transition proteins (TNPs) constitute 90% of the chromatin basic proteins during the steps of spermiogenesis between histone removal and the deposition of the protamines. TNP2 is closely linked to the protamine (PRM) genes suggesting that they arose by gene duplication and might have retained common functions. In contrast, TNP1 is on a separate chromosome.

nodes.name: Succinate-CoA ligase subunits
nodes.description: Succinate-CoA ligase (SUCL) is a mitochondrial enzyme that catalyses the reversible conversion of succinyl-CoA and ADP or GDP to succinate and ATP or GTP. SUCL is composed of an alpha subunit, encoded by SUCLG1, and a beta subunit, encoded by either SUCLA2 or SUCLG2. The alpha subunit forms a heterodimer with either of its beta subunits, resulting in an ADP-forming SUCL (A-SUCL)(EC 6.2.1.5) and a GDP-forming SUCL (G-SUCL)(EC 6.2.1.4), respectively. The beta subunits thus determine the substrate specificity of the enzymes.

nodes.name: ATP-grasp fold containing
nodes.description: The ATP-grasp fold is an atypical ATP-binding site comprised of two alpha and beta domains that 'grasp' a molecule of ATP between them. Members of the family typically have an overall structural design containing 3 common conserved focal domains. Most members catalyze the ATP-assisted reaction of a carboxylic acid with a nucleophile via the formation of an acylphosphate intermediate but there enzymes that catalyze only the phosphoryl transfer step and thus are kinases instead of ligases. Members of the ATP-grasp superfamily are found in several metabolic pathways including de novo purine biosynthesis, gluconeogenesis and fatty acid synthesis.

nodes.name: Ribosomal modification protein rimK like family
nodes.description: Mammalian genomes contain two genes homologous to Escherichia coli RIMK, which ligates glutamates to the C terminus of ribosomal protein S6. One of them, named RIMKLA, is almost exclusively expressed in the CNS, whereas RIMKLB, which shares 65% sequence identity with RIMKLA, is expressed in CNS and testis. RIMKLA catalyzes the ATP-dependent synthesis of N-acetylaspartylglutamate (NAAG), the most abundant dipeptide present in vertebrate central nervous system (CNS), from N-acetylaspartate and l-glutamate. RIMKLB catalyzes this reaction as well as the synthesis of β-citrylglutamate, a structural analogue of NAAG present in testis and immature brain.

nodes.name: Mitogen-activated protein kinase 8-10 (JNK) family
nodes.description: The c-Jun N-terminal kinases (JNKs) are a closely related subgroup of enzymes in the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) family comprising MAPK8 (JNK1), MAPK9 (JNK2) and MAPK10 (JNK3). NKs) JNKs phosphorylate and activate members of the activator protein-1 (AP-1) transcription factor family and other cellular factors implicated in regulating altered gene expression, cellular survival and proliferation in response to cytokines and growth factors, noxious stimuli and oncogenic transformation.

nodes.name: Atypical mitogen-activated protein kinases
nodes.description: Mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinases are a family of serine/threonine kinases that play a central role in transducing extracellular cues into a variety of intracellular responses ranging from lineage specification to cell division and adaptation. MAP kinases can be classified into conventional or atypical enzymes, based on their ability to get phosphorylated and activated by members of the MAP kinase kinase (MAP2K)/MEK family. Atypical MAP kinases are not activated by MAP2Ks.

nodes.name: Conventional mitogen-activated protein kinases
nodes.description: Mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinases are a family of serine/threonine kinases that play a central role in transducing extracellular cues into a variety of intracellular responses ranging from lineage specification to cell division and adaptation. MAP kinases can be classified into conventional or atypical enzymes, based on their ability to get phosphorylated and activated by members of the MAP kinase kinase (MAP2K)/MEK family. Conventional MAP kinases are part of the mitogen-activated protein kinases cascade. They have the distinctive feature of a Thr–Xaa–Tyr motif in the activation loop, which is the site of activating phosphorylation by the MAP2K family members MAP2K1–7.

nodes.name: Mitogen-activated protein kinase 11-14 (p38) family
nodes.description: MAPK11, MAPK12, MAPK13 AND MAPK14 constitute a subfamily of conventional mitogen-activated kinases, also commonly known as the p38 MAPK family, that are strongly activated by various environmental stresses including oxidative stress, UV irradiation, hypoxia, ischemia, inflammatory cytokines, GPCRs, and Rho family GTPases. In addition to the usual activation by two upstream MAP2Ks, MAP2K3 (MKK3) and MAP2K6 (MKK6), the p38 MAPKs can also be activated by binding of TAB1 or phosphorylation by the tyrosine kinases ZAP70 and LCK. MAP2K3/6 are activated by several MAP3Ks. All p38 MAPKs are activated in response to appropriate stimuli by dual phosphorylation in the activation loop sequence Thr-Gly-Tyr. p38 MAPKs play critical roles in a wide variety of cellular processes such as proliferation, differentiation, regeneration, and metabolism.

nodes.name: Mitogen-activated protein kinase 3 and 1 (ERK1/2) family
nodes.description: The evolutionarily conserved kinases MAPK1 and MAPK3, also known as ERK2 and ERK1 respectively, constituye one of the four subfamilies of conventional MAPKs. Activation of each group of conventional MAPKs depends on a set of two upstream, evolutionarily conserved, sequentially acting kinases. MAPK1/3 are activated by growth factors, ligands for heterotrimeric G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), cytokines, osmotic stress, microtubule disorganization, and in response to insulin. Their main initiating kinases (MAP3Ks) are members of the RAF family, which include serine/threonine-protein kinases ARAF, BRAF and RAF1 (CRAF), and are often activated as a result of their interaction with active GTP-bound RAS proteins. Once activated, RAF kinases phosphorylate and activate components of the MAP2K module, such as MAP2K1 (MEK1) and MAP2K2 (MEK2), which in turn activate MAPK1 and MAPK3 through phosphorylation of both tyrosine and threonine residues present in a conserved tripeptide motif (Thr-Glu-Tyr) within their activation loop. Through the phosphorylation of their targets, MAPK1 and MAPK3 are involved in a wide variety of cellular processes including proliferation, inflammation, and cellular metabolism.

nodes.name: Prostaglandin E synthases
nodes.description: Prostaglandin E synthases (PGESs) (EC:5.3.99.3) convert cyclooxygenase (COX)-derived prostaglandin H2 (PGH2) into prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) and comprise three types of structurally and biologically distinct enzymes. Two of these, namely PGES (mPGES-1) and PGES2 (mPGES-2), are membrane-bound enzymes. PGES is an inflammation-inducible enzyme that converts PGH2 into PGE2. PGES2 is a bifunctional enzyme that generally forms a complex with haem in the presence of glutathione. This enzyme can metabolise PGH2 into malondialdehyde and can produce PGE2 after its separation from haem. PGES3 (cPGES) is a constitutive cytosolic enzyme.

nodes.name: Secernin family
nodes.description: The secernins are a family of peptidase domain containing proteins. SCRN1 regulates exocytosis in mast cells and SCRN3 is involved in thermal nociception.

nodes.name: Unc-51 like kinase family
nodes.description: Serine–threonine protein kinases of the Unc-51 like kinase (ULK) family are found across eukaryotic species, with the best-characterized members found in metazoans and plants. In mammals the family has four active kinases (ULK1, ULK2, ULK3, and STK36 (Fused homolog) and one pseudokinase (ULK4). The active kinases function in multiple well-studied biological processes: ULK1 and ULK2 act in autophagy pathways in starvation responses, ULK3 is a regulator of the sonic hedgehog signaling pathway, and Fused kinase was first identified in Drosophila as a kinase of the Hedgehog (Hh) signaling pathway. Studies in the flagellated protist Leishmania mexicana show the pseudokinase ULK4 is a positive regulator of STK36 in a pathway required for stable assembly of motile cilia.

nodes.name: MST kinase family
nodes.description: The mammalian MST kinase family, which is related to the Hippo kinase in Drosophila melanogaster, includes five related proteins: STK4 (MST1), STK3 (MST2), STK24 (MST3), STK26 (MST4), and STK25 (also called YSK1 or SOK1). MST kinases are key signaling molecules that influence cell proliferation, organ size, cell migration, and cell polarity.

nodes.name: Germinal centre like kinase family
nodes.description: The STE20 related kinases are divided into two major groups based on the location of the catalytic domain: 5′ or N-terminal for the germinal center like kinases (GCKs) and 3′ or C-terminal for the p21-activated kinases (PAKs).

nodes.name: MAP4K family (GCK-IV subfamily)
nodes.description: The mitogen-activated kinase kinase kinase kinases (MAP4Ks) are split across two subfamilies. There are 4 members of the GCK-IV subfamily.

nodes.name: MAP4K family (GCK-I subfamily)
nodes.description: The mitogen-activated kinase kinase kinase kinases (MAP4Ks) are split across two subfamilies. The GCK-I subfamily of Ste20 kinases comprises four MAP4Ks that activate the JNK/SAPK pathway.

nodes.name: Casein kinase 1 and related kinase families
Casein kinase 2 subunits
nodes.description: Casein kinase 2 (CK2 or CK-II) is one of the first identified protein kinases. It phosphorylates hundreds of physiological substrates, and is one of the major contributors to the generation of the human phospho-proteome. Structurally, mammalian CK2 is a tetrameric enzyme, composed of two catalytic and two regulatory subunits. The catalytic ones might be represented either by alpha or alpha prime, very similar but encoded by two different genes, CSNK2A1 and CSNK2A2, respectively, while only one human CK2 regulatory subunit exists, beta, encoded by the CSNK2B gene. The regulatory functions of beta are limited to preserving the enzyme stability and driving the selection of substrates. In fact, CK2 is constitutively active, and catalytically competent also in its monomeric form.

nodes.name: Casein kinase 2 alpha family
nodes.description: The Casein kinase 2 alpha family encodes the catalytic subunits of CK2. Structurally, mammalian CK2 is a tetrameric enzyme, composed of two catalytic and two regulatory subunits. The catalytic ones might be represented either by alpha or alpha prime, very similar but encoded by two different genes, CSNK2A1 and CSNK2A2. CSNK2A3 also has the potential to function as catalytic subunit of CK2. It is an intronless retrogene that encodes a protein with 98% identity to CSNK2A1 that was previously annotated as a pseudogene (CSNK2A1P).

nodes.name: Casein kinase 2 beta family
nodes.description: The Casein kinase 2 beta family encodes the single regulatory beta subunit of CK2. There is only one human CK2 regulatory subunit encoded by the CSNK2B gene. The regulatory functions of CSNK2B are limited to preserving the enzyme stability and driving the selection of substrates.

nodes.name: Neurensin family
nodes.description: The paralogous genes of the Neurensin family, NRSN1 and NRSN2, encode small transmembrane proteins that share around 30% protein identity. Expression of NRSN1 is restricted to brain whereas NRSN2, while enriched in brain, has a much wider expression pattern. Mouse neurensin 1 has been shown to play roles in the transport of small vesicles to the growing distal end of neurites in association with microtubules, thereby contributing to neurite extension.

nodes.name: Thymosin beta family
nodes.description: The Thymosin betas are a family of highly conserved polar 5 kDa peptides originally thought to be thymic hormones. Thymosin beta 4 as well as other members of this ubiquitous peptide family were identified as the main intracellular G-actin sequestering peptides, being present in high concentrations in almost every cell. Thymosins betas bind monomeric actin in a 1:1 complex and act as actin buffers, preventing polymerization into actin filaments but supplying a pool of actin monomers when the cell needs filaments.

nodes.name: SLAIN family
nodes.description: From studies in mouse, paralogs SLAIN1 and SLAIN2 have been identified as microtubule plus-end tracking proteins that act as regulators of microtubule dynamics. SLAINs are targeted to microtubule tips through an interaction with the core components of microtubule plus-end tracking protein network, Microtubule associated protein RP/EB family members. SLAINs promote persistent microtubule growth by recruiting the microtubule polymerase CKAP5 (ch-TOG) to microtubule plus-ends.

nodes.name: Cyclin dependent kinase like family
nodes.description: CDK-like proteins cluster together in a separate branch from the CDK family close to MAP kinases and GSK3 kinases.

nodes.name: Neuropilin family
nodes.description: Neuropilins are highly conserved single pass transmembrane proteins specific to vertebrates. They were originally identified as adhesion molecules in the nervous system, but were subsequently rediscovered as the ligand binding subunit of the class 3 semaphorin receptor in neurons and then as blood vessel receptors for the vascular endothelial growth factor VEGF. The two human two neuropilins (NRP1 and NRP2), are paralogs with 44% amino acid identity and identical domain structures. The large extracellular domain contains two complement-binding homology domains and two coagulation factor V/VIII homology domains, that are crucial for ligand binding, and a meprin domain. The meprin domain domain and transmembrane domain promote receptor dimerisation. The intracellular domain contains a motif that binds PDZ-domain containing proteins. As a result of this complex domain structure, neuropilins bind multiple ligands and associate with several different types of co-receptors variably promoting cell adhesion, repulsion or attraction.

nodes.name: Neuropilin and tolloid like family
nodes.description: The Neuropilin and tolloid like family (NETO1 and NETO2) encode type-1 transmembrane proteins containing two CUB domains and one LDLa domain in the extracellular domain and a PDZ binding motifs at their C-terminal. They function as Kainate receptor (KAR) auxiliary subunits.

nodes.name: Akirin family
nodes.description: Akirins are small, highly conserved, primarily nuclear proteins that play critical regulators of multiple developmental processes by acting as modulators of gene expression patterns. Akirins have been shown to have essential roles in interdigital regression during limb development, in the immune system, during neural development and in muscle development and function.

nodes.name: Fasciculation and elongation protein zeta family
nodes.description: The fasciculation and elongation protein zeta family (FEZ1 and FEZ2) are the homologs of C. elegans unc-76, a gene involved in axonal growth. FEZ proteins are implicated in intracellular transport, acting as bivalent cargo transport adaptors in kinesin-mediated movement.

nodes.name: FXYD domain containing ion transport regulators
Ataxin 1 family
nodes.description: ATXN1 (ataxin 1) and ATXN1L (ataxin 1 like) are paralogous genes encoding nuclear proteins that function primarily as transcriptional regulators within multiprotein chromatin complexes. Their molecular functions are best understood through shared interaction partners (especially CIC) and genetic studies showing partial redundancy. Expansions of a polyglutamine tract in ATXN1 are associated with Spinocerebellar ataxia 1.

nodes.name: Ataxin 2 family
nodes.description: ATXN2 and ATXN2L are paralogs that encode proteins contain Lsm and LsmAD domains for binding to RNA, and a PAM2 motif for interaction with PABP. Expansions of a polygluatamine tract in ATXN2 cause spinocerebellar ataxia 2 (SCA2). The polygluatamine tract is not found in ATXN2L.  ATXN2 protein is involved in mRNA degradation, stability, and translation by modulating the PABP protein, 3′ untranslated regions, and stress granule and P-body formation. ATXN2L is involved in stress granule and RNA metabolism.

nodes.name: Ataxin 3 family
nodes.description: ATXN3 AND ATXN3L contain an N-terminal catalytic Josephin domain and two or three UIM motifs. Expansions of a polyglutamine tract in ATXN3 are associated with Spinocerebellar ataxia 3; ATXN3L also has a polyglutamine tract but unlike ATXN3 it does not appear to expand.

nodes.name: Ataxin 7 family
nodes.description: ATXN7 is a component of the SAGA complex. It is part of the deubiquitinase module (DUBm) and functions as the structural anchor that links the DUBm to the larger SAGA complex. PolyQ-expanded ATXN7 forms nuclear aggregates that are thought to sequester other components of the DUBm such that the complex can no longer remove ubiquitin from its substrates.   ATXN7 has four paralogs, none of which have an expandable polyQ tract. ATXN7L3 is another component of the SAGA DUBm; it cooperates with ENYS to form a stable interaction with the catalytic deubiquitinase USP22. ATXN7L3B encodes a much shorter protein that can also interact with ENY2 of the DUBm, however it seems to only function to limit SAGA activity by competing with ATXN7L3. ATXN7L1 and ATXN7L2 have highly conserved domains with ATXN7 and they may play an interchangeable role in SAGA DUBm.

nodes.name: Fibroblast growth factor binding protein family
nodes.description: Fibroblast growth factor binding proteins (FGFBPs) affect a plethora of biological processes by modulating the actions of FGF ligands. Three paralogous genes encoding FGFBPs (FGFBP1, FGFBP2 and FGFBP3) are present in humans and other species. Rodents, however, are an exception to this as they lack an FGFBP2 gene locus. Additionally, FGFBP2 is produced in lymphoid tissues, where it appears to modulate immune responses. Despite the evolutionary divergence of these three genes, FGFBPs are highly homologous across species. Each contains a signal sequence for secretion as well as binding sites for heparin and FGF ligands. These structural features allow FGFBPs to reversibly bind and increase the bioavailability of FGF ligands. FGFBPs are presumed to augment signaling by chaperoning FGFs through the ECM to FGFRs.

nodes.name: Regulator of calcineurin family
nodes.description: The Regulator of calcineurin family act as endogenous inhibitors of calcineurin, a calcium-dependent protein phosphatase. They regulate crucial cellular processes, such as T-cell activation and the NFAT (nuclear factor of activated T-cells) signalling pathway.  The three members of this family, RCAN1, RCAN2 and RCAN3, are paralogs. RCAN1 is located on chromosome 21, and its over expression in Down syndrome contributes to the phenotype.

nodes.name: MIER complex subunits
nodes.description: HDAC complexes repress gene transcription through removing acetyl groups from lysine residues in histone tails. In addition to the deacetylase subunit, these complexes typically contain transcription factor and/or chromatin binding activities. The MIER:HDAC complex has hitherto been poorly characterized. MIER1 unexpectedly co-purifies with an H2A:H2B histone dimer and is also able to bind a complete histone octamer. A larger MIER1:HDAC1:BAHD1:C1QBP complex additionally co-purifies with an intact nucleosome on which H3K27 is either di- or tri-methylated. Together this suggests that the MIER1 complex acts downstream of PRC2 to expand regions of repressed chromatin and could potentially deposit histone octamer onto nucleosome-depleted regions of DNA.

nodes.name: RERE complex subunits
nodes.description: The transcriptional regulator RERE/Atrophin-2 (RERE) is required for the normal patterning of the early vertebrate embryo, including the central nervous system, pharyngeal arches, and limbs. Consistent with a role as a transcriptional corepressor, RERE binds histone deacetylase 1 and 2 (HDAC1/2), and orphan nuclear receptors such as Tlx (approved symbol NR2E1).

nodes.name: SERTA domain containing
nodes.description: The SERTA (for SEI-1, RBT-1, and TARA) domain is a motif of ~47 residues corresponding to the largest conserved region among TRIP-Br (transcriptional regulator interacting with the PHD-bromodomain) proteins, an evolutionarily conserved family restricted to higher eukaryotes. In SERTAD1-3 and CDCA4, the SERTA domain is found in association with a cyclin A-binding domain, a PHD-bromo binding domain and a conserved C-terminal region. In contrast, SERTAD4 shares only the SERTA and cyclin A-binding domains with other SERTADs.

nodes.name: Sarcoglycans
nodes.description: The sarcoglycans are transmembrane proteins found in the plasma membrane of muscle cells. Sarcoglycans assemble into the sarcoglycan complex, a subcomplex within the dystrophin glycoprotein complex (DGC) that associates with dystrophin and mediates muscle membrane stability. Each of the six human sacrcoglycan genes is encoded by eight identically placed exons, consistent with preserved gene structure and multiple gene duplication events. Mutations in sarcoglycan genes lead to muscular dystrophy and cardiomyopathy in both humans and mice.

nodes.name: Roundabout guidance receptor family
nodes.description: Named after the Drosophila roundabout mutant phenotype, in which many more axons reach the midline and cross it abnormally following a circular trajectory, the family of four mammalian roundabout guidance receptors (ROBOs) have a conserved role in axon guidance. ROBOs are single-pass transmembrane receptors belonging to a subfamily of the immunoglobulin (Ig) superfamily proteins and typically act as receptors for the Slit family of guidance ligands. ROBO3 does not bind SLITs with high affinity due to specific alterations in its first immunoglobulin domain but still plays a role in axon guidance through interaction with the ligand NELL2.

nodes.name: Slit guidance ligands
nodes.description: The Slit family encode extracellular matrix-secreted glycoproteins that act as guidance molecules, helping growing axons find their targets during nervous system development. Slit action is mediated mainly by the Roundabout guidance receptor family of single pass transmembrane proteins, although it has been shown that other proteins can also function as Slit receptors.

nodes.name: Hyaluronan and proteoglycan link protein family
nodes.description: Hyaluronan and proteoglycan link proteins are a family of extracellular glycoproteins that help stabilize the extracellular matrix (ECM) by linking hyaluronan (HA) to Hyalectan proteoglycans (Lecticans) family members: aggrecan, versican, brevican, and neurocan.

nodes.name: Mex-3 RNA binding family
nodes.description: The MEX3 family encode proteins that contain two heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein K homology (KH) domains and one carboxy-terminal RING finger module. They are phosphoproteins that bind RNA through their KH domains and shuttle between the nucleus and the cytoplasm via the CRM1-dependent export pathway. They show differential localization to cytosolic foci identified as sites of mRNA storage, translation regulation and degradation. The genes were named based on homology to the C. elegans Mex-3 gene.

nodes.name: Coagulation factors
nodes.description: Blood coagulation involves a complex yet regulated cascade of over two dozen proteins in blood. Most of these proteins are serine protease enzymes and circulate in blood as inactive zymogens waiting for an activation trigger such as proteolytic cleavage. For coagulation, this trigger is usually some form of vascular injury, followed by activation. In the classical waterfall model, each activated protein goes on to activate the next protein in a rapidly expanding cascade of reactions which quickly results in the local formation of a fibrin clot to seal the injury. The 11 human coagulation factor proteins in blood are usually indicated by F and a Roman numeral and followed by a lowercase 'a' to indicate their active form, namely FG, FII, FIII, FV, FVII, FVIII, FIX, FX, FXI, FXII, and FXIII. FG is comprised of the alpha, beta, and gamma genes of fibrinogen (FG) (FGA, FGB, and FGG) while FXIII is produced from two genes F13A1 and F13B. Thus these 11 coagulation factor proteins are produced by 14 genes.

nodes.name: Decarboxylases
nodes.description: Decarboxylases are enzyme that catalyze the removal of a carboxyl group (–COOH) from a molecule, usually releasing it as carbon dioxide. This group represents the enzymes with EC 4.1.1.- enzyme commission numbers.

nodes.name: Antizyme inhibitor family
nodes.description: The antizyme inhibitors (AZIN1 and AZIN2) regulate the function of ornithine decarboxylase (ODC). ODC is one of the two rate-limiting enzymes of polyamine biosynthesis. AZINs are homolgous to ODC but do not have decarboxylase activity. AZINs compete with OCD to bind ornithine decarboxylase antizymes (OAZs). OAZs inhibit OCD by blocking ODC homodimerization.

nodes.name: Ornithine decarboxylase antizyme family
nodes.description: Ornithine decarboxylase antizymes decrease polyamine levels via three mechanisms: inhibiting ornithine decarboxylase (ODC), the key enzyme catalyzing the first and rate-limiting step in polyamine biosynthesis, by disrupting the active ODC homodimers; targeting ODC monomers for ubiquitin-independent degradation by the 26S proteasome; and inhibiting polyamine transporter-mediated polyamine uptake into cells. The OAZ1-3 genes are structurally similar and all three antizymes inhibit ODC activity and polyamine uptake. OAZ1 and OAZ2 are ubiquitously expressed in somatic tissues, while OAZ3 is expressed in a tissue and cell-specific manner, predominantly in the haploid germ cells in testis. All vertebrate OAZs are encoded by two partially overlapping open reading frames (ORFs): a short ORF1 with a translation initiation codon and an in-frame stop codon at the frameshift site; and a longer ORF2, which lacks a start codon, that is in +1 frame with respect to ORF1, and encodes a larger portion of the antizyme protein. Therefore, the synthesis of full-length, functional antizyme requires translation initiation at the ORF1 start codon, followed by +1 ribosomal frameshift just before the ORF1 stop codon, and translation termination at the ORF2 stop codon. The +1 ribosomal frameshifting is stimulated by polyamines.

nodes.name: Beclin family
nodes.description: The two members of the Beclin family are paralogs that share a high degree of amino acid sequence similarity but have divergent N-terminal regions. Beclin 1 regulates autophagy and is involved in initiating the formation of autophagosomes in cells. It is a component of the class III PI3K complex that is responsible for generating phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI3P) at the site of membrane formation. Beclin 2 promotes endosomal-mediated degradation of GASP1-dependent GPCRs. It is also an inhibitor of innate immune signaling pathways to suppress the production of proinflammatory cytokines. Similar to Beclin 1, Beclin 2 has been implicated in regulating autophagy and is reported to interact with components in the class III PI3K complex.

nodes.name: CBP/p300-interacting transactivator with ED-rich tail family
nodes.description: There are three members of the CBP/p300-interacting transactivator with ED-rich tail (CITED) family in human, CITED1, CITED2 and CITED4. CITED3 is present in avian, amphibian, and fish species but absent in mice and humans. CITED proteins function as co-activators or repressors by regulating CBP/p300:transcription factor complex formation. They lack DNA binding domains and are not known to form dimers or multimers. Instead, these proteins contain sets of conserved region (CR) motifs including a C-terminal domain (48-55 aa) common to all CITED proteins. Outside the conserved regions, CITED proteins exhibit minimal sequence similarity and are largely unstructured, but can contain protein interaction motifs, such as the Smad-interacting domain (SID) identified in CITED1.

nodes.name: Basic charge Y-linked 2 family
nodes.description: The Basic charge Y-linked family consists of three protein coding genes (BPY2, BPY2B and BPY2C) and one pseudogene (BPY2DP). The basic proteins encoded by this family are identical. BPY2, BPY2B and BPY2C are located in the azoospermia (AZFc) factor c region. AZFc is the most commonly deleted region of the AZF locus in infertile men.

nodes.name: Shugoshin family
nodes.description: Shugoshins are evolutionarily conserved proteins that function to protect sister chromatid cohesion, thus ensuring chromosomal stability during mitosis and meiosis in eukaryotes. Members of the Shugoshin family all contain two conserved domains: namely, the N-terminal coiled coil structure believed to mediate homodimerization and interaction with other proteins and the C-terminal basic region required for its chromosomal localization.

nodes.name: Cylicin family
nodes.description: Cylicins are testis-specific proteins, which are exclusively expressed during spermiogenesis. In humans and mice, two Cylicins, the gonosomal X-linked cylicin 1 (CYLC1) and the autosomal cylicin 2 (CYLC2) genes, have been identified. CYLC2 has a much shorter amino-terminal portion than CYLC1. Cylicins are cytoskeletal proteins with an overall positive charge due to lysine-rich repeats with a predominant localization in the calyx of mature sperm. Phenotypical characterization revealed that loss of Cylicins prevents proper calyx assembly during spermiogenesis.

nodes.name: Epithelial splicing regulatory protein family
nodes.description: The Epithelial splicing regulatory proteins (ESRP1 and ESRP2) are closely related sequence-specific RNA binding proteins (RBPs) that control alternative splicing of a large number of genes, coordinating epithelial-mesenchymal transitions (EMTs) that are critical for organismal development and cancer progression.

nodes.name: Cryptochrome circadian regulator family
nodes.description: Cryptochrome circadian regulators (CRY1 and CRY2) are essential components of the mammalian circadian clock as the transcriptional repressors in transcription-translation negative feedback loops (TTFLs). CRYs together with Period circadian regulators (PERs) form a large complex in the cytoplasm, translocate into the nucleus, and suppress the transcriptional activity of the CLOCK–BMAL1 heterodimer. PER and CRY are subsequently degraded through the ubiquitin–proteasome pathway to alleviate CLOCK–BMAL1 repression, allowing initiation of a new circadian cycle. This negative feedback loop underlies the ~24-h oscillatory pattern that forms the core of circadian timekeeping.  CRYs comprises two structural subdomains: the photolyase homology region (PHR) and the C-terminal tail. The PHR includes the flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) pocket binding to FAD and the secondary pocket binding to CLOCK. The PHR is highly ordered with ~80% sequence identity between CRY1 and CRY2.

nodes.name: NGFI-A binding protein family
nodes.description: NGFI-A binding corepressors NAB1 and NAB2 interact with a conserved domain (R1 domain) within the EGR1 (aka NGFI-A) and EGR2 (aka KROX20) transactivators, and repress the transcription of EGR target promoters.

nodes.name: GCM transcription factor family
nodes.description: GCM proteins constitute a small transcription factor family with a DNA-binding domain exhibiting a novel fold composed of two subdomains rigidly held together by coordination of one of two structural zinc cations. In all known cases, GCM proteins exert the role of master regulators: the prototypical family member determines gliogenesis in Drosophila melanogaster, whereas mammalian GCM proteins orchestrate divergent aspects of development and physiology in placenta, kidney, thymus, and parathyroid gland.

nodes.name: Doublesex and mab-3 related transcription factor family
nodes.description: DMRT proteins are defined by a DNA-binding region called the DM domain. This motif was named after the founding members dsx in Drosophila and mab-3 in C. elegans. Both genes encode transcription factors that perform analogous functions in sexual development. The DM domain encodes an intertwined zinc-finger like DNA-binding motif, followed by an alpha-helical recognition domain that confers sequence-specific DNA binding through a 13 bp pseudo-palindromic DNA motif.  DMRT proteins regulate the transcription of target genes by activation or repression. They can form heterodimers on DNA in vitro and in vivo, raising the possibility that they may interact functionally by forming mixed complexes.  DMRTC1 AND DMRTC1B are tandemly duplicated genes on the X chromosome that encode identical proteins. Although related to other DMRT proteins, DMRTC1 AND DMRTC1B do not contain a canonical DM DNA-binding domain.

nodes.name: Grainyhead like transcription factor family
nodes.description: The mammalian homologs of the D. melanogaster grainyhead gene (grh), grainyhead like transcription factor 1–3 (GRHL1, GRHL2 and GRHL3), are transcription factors implicated in wound healing, tubulogenesis and cancer. GRHL1, 2 and 3 contain an N-terminal transcriptional activation domain, a central CP2 DNA-binding domain with structural similarities to p53, and a C-terminal dimerization domain with ubiquitin-like folds. The GRHL proteins are able to homo- and hetero-dimerize.

nodes.name: Transcription factor CP2 family
nodes.description: TFCP2, TFCP2L1 and UBP1 encode a family of transcription factors that are closely related to the grainyhead like transcription factors.

nodes.name: TFCP2/GRHL transcription factor family
nodes.description: The transcription factors of the TFCP2/GRHL family are characterized by the possession of a distinctive DNA-binding domain that bears no clear relationship to other known DNA-binding domains, with the possible exception of the p53 core domain. The family is split into the TFCP2 subfamily and the GRHL subfamily, which can be distinguished by their distinctive oligomerization domains and differences in their oligomerization behavior. Grainyhead (GRH) binds to DNA as a dimer, whereas TFCP2 binds as a tetramer. The DNA binding regions in both protein subfamilies show a large amount of conservation, but each has distinct transcriptional targets.

nodes.name: Signal transducer and activator of transcription family
nodes.description: All the STAT transcription factors share similar N-terminal, coiled-coil, DNA-binding, linker, SH2, and transactivation domains. In general, activated JAKs phosphorylate the conserved tyrosine residue of one STAT monomer, which then binds to the SH2 domain of another monomer, driving a conformational change that enables STATs to translocate into the nucleus to initiate the transcription of target genes.

nodes.name: Achaete-scute family bHLH transcription factors
nodes.description: The achaete-scute complex-like (ASCL) gene family consists of five members, namely ASCL1, ASCL2, ASCL3, ASCL4, and ASCL5. Dysregulation of ASCL family genes has been reported to play a key role in psychiatric and neurological disorders. All ASCL genes encode the basic helix-loop-helix transcription factors that control nervous system development; thus, they are called proneural genes. Expression of ASCL family genes and the impact of their products on cells are not limited to the nervous system. For example, ASCL family members have been shown to be expressed in progenitor cells during muscle and intestinal-cell differentiation.

nodes.name: Inhibitor of DNA binding family
nodes.description: Mammals have four ID proteins, ID1 to ID4, that share extensive sequence homology in the helix-loop-helix (HLH) motif, which mediates the dimerization of ID proteins with basic HLH proteins, primarily the group of E proteins encoded by TCF3 (E2A), TCF4 (E2-2) and TCF12. Because ID proteins do not have the basic amino acids necessary for DNA binding, they serve as naturally occurring dominant-negative inhibitors of E proteins by forming nonfunctional heterodimers. Outside of the HLH motif, there is little similarity among the four proteins.

nodes.name: Hey bHLH transcription factor family
nodes.description: The vertebrate Hey proteins are basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) transcription factors that are closely related to the Hes family of proteins and the Drosophila hairy and Enhancer of split genes. They are integral members of the Notch signaling pathway, a central signaling system in embryonic development, differentiation processes, and later tissue homeostasis.

nodes.name: CREB1 transcription factor family
nodes.description: The cyclic AMP response element (CRE)-binding protein (CREB) 1 family of activators functions in diverse physiological processes, including the control of cellular metabolism and growth-factor-dependent cell survival. Consistent with these diverse functions, CREB1 and its paralogs ATF1 and CREM are activated by phosphorylation in response to a number of signalling pathways, including cAMP, calcium, stress and mitogenic stimuli.  CREB1 and ATF1 proteins are both expressed ubiquitously, whereas CREM is expressed at highest levels in neuroendocrine tissues. The primary structure of the CREB1 family of activators reveals a centrally located 60-amino-acid kinase-inducible domain (KID), which contains the PKA phosphorylation site (RRPSY) as well as several potential phosphorylation sites for casein kinases I and II. The KID is flanked by hydrophobic glutamine-rich domains, designated Q1 and Q2, which function as constitutive activators in vitro. A basic region/leucine zipper (bZIP) dimerization domain is located carboxy-terminally in all family members.

nodes.name: Cap 'n' collar bZIP transcription factors
nodes.description: In mammals, the cap 'n' collar (CNC) family of transcription factors comprises six proteins: NFE, NFE2L1, NFE2L2, NFE2L3, BACH1 and BACH2. All six proteins share a common CNC sequence adjacent to a DNA binding domain. CNC proteins bind a common DNA motif termed the antioxidant response element (ARE). Mammalian CNC transcription factors cannot regulate gene expression as monomers. Canonically, these proteins heterodimerize with small MAF transcription factors (MAFF, MAFK, and MAFG) to regulate transcription.

nodes.name: BACH transcriptional regulator family
nodes.description: The BTB And CNC Homology (Bach) family consists of BACH1 and BACH2, which encode transcription factors that belongs to the Cap'n'Collar type of the basic region-leucine zipper factor family. Small Maf proteins are bZip proteins that form dimers capable of either activating or repressing transcription. BACH1 and BACH2 form heterodimers with small Maf proteins that binds to the Maf recognition element (MARE) to act as transcription repressors. In addition, BACH proteins possess a BTB/POZ domain (broad complex, tram track, bric-a-brac/poxvirus and zinc finger) located at the N-termini. These domains are required for interactions with other proteins.

nodes.name: Centriolar satellite proteins
nodes.description: Centriolar satellites are ubiquitous membrane-less organelles that have been implicated in a wide range of vital cellular processes, such as cilium formation and function, actin filament nucleation and organization, microtubule organization, cell cycle progression, proteasome activity, autophagy, aggresome formation, cellular stress response and neurogenesis.

nodes.name: Distal-less homeobox family
nodes.description: The mammalian DLX genes encode homeobox-type transcription factors and are physically organized as convergent bigene clusters. The paired DLX genes share tissue specificity in the expression profile. Genetic regulatory mechanisms, such as intergenic enhancer sharing between paired DLX genes, have been proposed to explain this conservation of bigene structure. All mammalian DLX genes have expression and function in developing craniofacial structures, especially in the first and second pharyngeal arches (branchial arches). Each DLX cluster (DLX1/2, DLX3/4, and DLX5/6) has overlapping, nested expression in the branchial arches which is called the 'DLX code' and plays a key role in organizing craniofacial structure and evolution.

nodes.name: Fat storage inducing transmembrane protein family
nodes.description: Fat storage inducing transmembrane proteins 1 and 2 (FITM1 and FITM2) are the human members of the evolutionarily conserved FITM protein family. These proteins reside in the ER and have six transmembrane domains with the N- and C-termini facing the cytosol. Overexpression of either FITM1 or FITM2 in mammalian cells in culture, or in vivo in murine liver and skeletal muscle, all results in the accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs). LDs are evolutionarily conserved organelles present nearly ubiquitously across a broad range of organisms, from bacteria to mammals. FITM1 and 2 bind directly to triacylglycerol (TG) to regulate the cytosolic budding of neutral lipid to form LDs.

nodes.name: DNA fragmentation factor subunits
nodes.description: Apoptotic DNA fragmentation, the hallmark of apoptosis, is mediated primarily by the nuclease DFFB (also known as CAD or DFF40). DFFB exists as a heterodimer with DFFA (also know as DFF45 or ICAD), which is a specific chaperone and inhibitor of DFFB under normal conditions.

nodes.name: DRAM autophagy modulator family
nodes.description: The five members of the evolutionarily conserved DRAM family have all been shown be involved in autophagy regulation.

nodes.name: Activating transcription factor 4 family
nodes.description: ATF4 and ATF5 are paralogous bZIP transcription factors that integrate various stress signals. ATF4 and ATF5 share a secondary basic motif at the C-terminus that has been shown to be key for interdomain coupling between the transactivation and bZIP domains of ATF4.

nodes.name: Activating transcription factor 2 family
nodes.description: ATF2, ATF7 and CREB5 are paralogous bZIP transcription factors.

nodes.name: Activating transcription factor 3 family
nodes.description: ATF3 and JDP2 are paralogous bZIP transcription factors.

nodes.name: GIPC PDZ domain containing family
nodes.description: The GIPC family encode closely related adaptor proteins involved in cell signaling and intracellular transport. Each member has a central PDZ domain flanked by GIPC-homology (GH) domains termed GH1 and GH2.

nodes.name: Transmembrane 4 L six family
nodes.description: Transmembrane 4 L six family encode homologous four-pass transmembrane proteins with similar topology. Physiologically, they regulate tissue differentiation, signal transduction pathways, cellular activation, proliferation, motility, adhesion, and angiogenesis.

nodes.name: Calcium/calmodulin dependent protein kinase kinase family
Numb-associated kinase family
nodes.description: The Numb-associated family of protein kinases (NAKs) constitute a diverse family in terms of Ser/Thr kinases in both their function and structure, sharing little conservation outside of the kinase domain and as low as 30% sequence identity across their kinase domains. They are named for similarity to the Drosophila protein Nak, which plays a role during asymmetric cell division through its association with Numb. Humans have four known homologs: AAK1, BMP2K (also known as BIKE), GAK, and STK16 (also known as MPSK1).

nodes.name: Discoidin domain receptor tyrosine kinase family
MET proto-oncogene, receptor tyrosine kinase family
Tyrosine kinase with immunoglobulin like and EGF like domains family
PDGFR, CSF1R, KIT, FLT3 receptor tyrosine kinase family
Platelet derived growth factor receptor family
Muscle associated receptor tyrosine kinase family
ALK and LTK receptor tyrosine kinase family
ROS proto-oncogene 1, receptor tyrosine kinase family
GA binding protein transcription factor subunits
nodes.description: GABP is unique among the more than 20 distinct mammalian ets factors because it, alone, is an obligate multimeric protein complex. It includes two distinct and unrelated proteins — GABPalpha and GABPbeta — which, together, form a tetrameric alpha2beta2 complex. Importantly, the DNA binding domain (DBD) is present in the alpha subunit, while the transcriptional activation domain (TAD) is encoded by the beta subunit genes (GABPB1 and GABPB2); both components are necessary to generate a functional complex. The presence of the TAD and DBD on separate proteins distinguishes GABP from most transcription factors and from all other ets factors. As the name implies, this transcription factor binds to DNA sequences that are rich in the nucleotides guanine and adenine — a characteristic of the ets transcription factor family.

nodes.name: Egl-9 family hypoxia inducible factors
nodes.description: The mammalian EGLN family contains three paralagous genes (EGLN1, EGLN2, and EGLN3) encoding prolyl hydroxylase isoforms that mediate the oxygen-dependent targeting of the transcription factor hypoxia inducible factor alpha to the proteosome.

nodes.name: Heme oxygenase family
nodes.description: Heme oxygenase is the rate limiting enzyme in the heme degradative pathway. It catalyzes the degradation of heme to biliverdin and carbon monoxide. Heme oxygenase consists of two isoenzymes, encoded by paralogous genes, an inducible enzyme HMOX1 and a constitutive enzyme HMOX2.

nodes.name: Oxygenases
nodes.description: Oxygenases are enzymes that catalyze the incorporation of one or more atoms from molecular oxygen (O₂) into a substrate.

nodes.name: MICAL oxygenase family
nodes.description: MICALs are large proteins (>1,000 amino acids) consisting of a highly conserved N-terminal flavoprotein monooxygenase, followed by several other notable regions, including a calponin homology domain, a LIM domain, a proline-rich region with PxxP ligands for SH3-domain containing proteins, and a region that shares homology to the alpha region of Ezrin, Radixin, and Moesin (ERM) proteins. MICALs specifically bind and oxidize F-actin to posttranslationally alter specific amino acids within filament subunits.

nodes.name: RAD23 nucleotide excision repair protein family
Oxidative stress induced growth inhibitor family
Prolyl 4-hydroxylase subunits
nodes.description: Collagen prolyl 4-hydroxylase (C-P4H) is a critical enzyme involved in collagen biosynthesis, mediating the hydroxylation of proline residues to ensure the stability of collagen and its integration into the extracellular matrix (ECM). C-P4H operates as an alpha2beta2 tetramer, comprising three isoenzymes distinguished by their catalytic alpha-subunits (P4HA1, P4HA2, P4HA3) and a common beta-subunit (P4HB).

nodes.name: Aspartate beta-hydroxylase domain containing
nodes.description: Aspartate beta-hydroxylase (ASPH) specifically hydroxylates one Asp or Asn residue in certain epidermal growth factor (EGF)-like domains of a number of proteins. A similar hydroxylase domain (IPR007803) is found in the uncharacterised proteins ASPHD1 and ASPHD2.

nodes.name: Growth arrest and DNA damage inducible family
Rho GDP dissociation inhibitor family
nodes.description: RHO-specific guanine nucleotide dissociation inhibitors (ARHGDIs, also commonly known as RHOGDIs) are a family of proteins that have key roles in the regulation of the RHO GTPases. They function as negative regulators of RHO GTPases, extracting them from membranes and preventing their activation.

nodes.name: Phosphofurin acidic cluster sorting protein family
nodes.description: The PACS family are membrane traffic regulators have roles in integrating membrane traffic with interorganellar communication and, in response to death signals, regulation of apoptotic programmes.

nodes.name: PDGF family ligands
nodes.description: There are four platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) genes (PDGFA, PDGFB, PDGFC and PDGFD). Biologically active (able to activate a PDGF receptor (PDGFR)) PDGF is a dimer of two PDGF protein chains. Extracellular, proteolytic processing is required for activation of some isoforms of PDGF (PDGF-C and PDGF-D), while this step occurs intracellularly for PDGF-A, PDGF-B and PDGF-AB. Thus while all PDGFs are produced by cells and secreted, some of them are secreted in a latent form and become active only after being processed by proteases such as tissue plasminogen, urokinase plasminogen activator, plasmin and matriptase. There are a total of 5 biologically active PDGF proteins because in addition to the four homodimers (PDGF-A, PDGF-B, PDGF-C and PDGF-D) of PDGF, there is one heterodimer, PDGF-AB.

nodes.name: NOVA alternative splicing regulator family
nodes.description: NOVA1 and NOVA2 are neuron-specific RNA-binding proteins essential for alternative splicing (AS), influencing neurodevelopment by regulating transcript diversity. These proteins recognize YCAY sequences on pre-mRNA, regulating exon inclusion or skipping, intron retention, and alternative polyadenylation. Despite their 75% sequence identity, NOVA1 and NOVA2 exhibit distinct spatiotemporal expression patterns and target specificities, with NOVA2 predominantly expressed in cortical regions and NOVA1 in the cerebellum and spinal cord. De novo truncating variants in NOVA2 are responsible for a severe neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD), characterized by intellectual developmental disorder, motor delay, autistic features, and corpus callosum hypoplasia.

nodes.name: Katanin subunit families
nodes.description: The Katanin family of microtubule-severing enzymes is critical for remodeling microtubule-based structures that influence cell division, motility, morphogenesis and signaling. Katanin is composed of a catalytic p60 subunit (A subunit, KATNA1) and a regulatory p80 subunit (B subunit, KATNB1). The mammalian genome also encodes two additional A-like subunits (KATNAL1 and KATNAL2) and one additional B-like subunit (KATNBL1).

nodes.name: Katanin catalytic subunit family
nodes.description: Katanins are microtubule-severing enzymes critical for remodeling microtubule-based structures that influence cell division, motility, morphogenesis and signaling. The canonical catalytic p60 subunit of katanin is encoded by KATNA1. There are two additional KATNA like genes in the human genome, KATNA1L1 and KATNA1L2. KATNA1 and KATNAL1 share a similar domain architecture with an N-terminal microtubule interacting and trafficking domain (MIT)1 followed by a coiled coil domain (CC), a AAA ATPase domain (AAA) and a C-terminal VPS4 domain (VPS4_C). In contrast, KATNAL2 only contains the AAA domain, lacks the MIT, CC and VPS_4 domains, and has an N-terminal LisH (LIS1 homology) domain. Because KATNAL2 harbors a AAA domain that is required for Katanin microtubule-severing activity, it is predicted to have a role in microtubule-severing but KATNAL2 lacks the MIT domain that is important for microtubule binding in other Katanin A subunits.

nodes.name: Katanin regulatory subunit family
nodes.description: Katanins are microtubule-severing enzymes critical for remodeling microtubule-based structures that influence cell division, motility, morphogenesis and signaling. The canonical regulatory p80 subunit of katanin is encoded by KATNB1. There is an additional KATNB1 like gene in the human genome, KATNBL1. Although KATNB1 and KATNBL1 both harbor a conserved C-terminal region (con80), only KATNB1 contains additional N-terminal proline-rich (Pro-rich) and WD40 domains that are absent in KATNBL1.

nodes.name: RNA decapping and exonuclease complex subunits
nodes.description: The RNA decapping and exonuclease complex removes the 7-methylguanosine cap at 5′ terminus of mature mRNAs and degrades the RNA. The catalytic hydrolase subunit is DCP2. In higher eukaryotes, including humans, two paralogous cofactor proteins, DCP1A and DCP1A, work with DCP2. The decapping complex exists in multiple configurations, and stoichiometry of DCP1A and DCP1B in the complex varies in these distinct configurations. The EDC3 and EDC4 subunits regulate the efficiency and kinetics of decapping.

nodes.name: PH domain containing endocytic trafficking adaptor family
nodes.description: The paralogs PHETA1 and PHETA2 encode regulators of endosomal trafficking, specifically for receptor recycling to endosomes and for cargo sorting to lysosomes. Both PHETA1 and PHETA2 have a C-terminal phenylalanine-histidine motif (F&H motif) that serves as a binding site for OCRL, encoded by a gene that is mutated in Lowe syndrome.

nodes.name: Stromal interaction molecule family
nodes.description: Stromal interaction molecules (STIM) are a distinct class of ubiquitously expressed single-pass transmembrane proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane. Together with ORAI ion channels in the plasma membrane (PM), they form the molecular basis of the calcium release-activated calcium (CRAC) channel. The two homologous human STIM genes (STIM1 and STIM2) each encode multiple isoforms.

nodes.name: Small EDRK-rich factor family
nodes.description: The Small Factor Rich in EDRK (SERF) protein family is characterized by high conservation and a substantial positive charge. SERF1A and SERF1B encode identical proteins SERF1. SERF1 and SERF2 proteins exhibit common features, characterized by a distinctive N-SERF domain (N-terminal domain consisting of approximately 35 residues) fused with a less conserved C-terminal domain (25–45 amino acids) rich in charged amino acids, with an average isoelectric point (pI) greater than 10. SERFs are believed to be closely linked to physiological processes related to protein aggregation, such as amyloid-like protein assembly. The N-terminal region is known to mediate interactions with amyloidogenic proteins and RNAs.

nodes.name: Scaffold attachment factor B family
nodes.description: The Scaffold attachment factor B family (SAFB1, SAFB2 and SLTM), which are highly conserved evolutionarily, were first identified on the basis of their ability to bind scaffold attachment region DNA elements, but attention has subsequently shifted to their RNA-binding and protein–protein interactions. These proteins are involved in the cellular stress response and other aspects of gene regulation. They also crucial roles in DNA repair, processing of mRNA and regulatory RNA, as well as in interaction with chromatin-modifying complexes.

nodes.name: Regenerating family
nodes.description: The Regenerating (REG) family are multifunctional proteins with pro-proliferative, anti-apoptotic, differentiation-inducing and bactericidal properties. There is high homology among the REG genes and a distinctive feature of Reg proteins is the C-type-like lectin domain (CTLD), which selectively binds a wide variety of ligands and carbohydrates. There is no human ortholog of mouse Reg2.

nodes.name: Purine rich element binding protein family
nodes.description: The Pur proteins are an ancient family of sequence-specific single-stranded nucleic acid-binding proteins. They bind a G-rich element in either single- or double-stranded nucleic acids and are capable of displacing the complementary C-rich strand. In humans Pur proteins are critical for myeloid cell development, muscle development, and brain development, including trafficking of mRNA to neuronal dendrites. Pur family members have been implicated in diseases as diverse as cancer, premature aging, and fragile-X syndrome.

nodes.name: Interleukin 10 family
nodes.description: The Interleukin 10 family of cytokines is integral to the regulation of innate immune responses, primarily by modulating inflammation and preserving tissue homeostasis especially at mucosal and epithelial interfaces. This family is comprised of IL10, IL19, IL20, IL22, IL24, and IL26 all of which exhibit structural similarities, share receptor components, and commonly signal through the JAK-STAT pathway, with STAT3 being the principal mediator.

nodes.name: Interleukin 2 family
nodes.description: The Interleukin 2 family (IL2, IL4, IL7, IL9, IL15, and IL21) play a critical role in immunity in both steady state and disease. They are type 1 four α-helical proteins that signal through the shared γc receptor subunit encoded by IL2RG. This family is often referred to as the common gamma chain (γc) cytokine family.

nodes.name: Interleukin 12 type subunits
nodes.description: The IL-12 family of cytokines is comprised of IL-12 (IL12A/IL12B), IL-23 (IL23A/IL12B), IL-27 (IL27/EBI3) and IL-35 (IL12A/EBI3) and has emerged as important regulators of host immunity. Each member is composed of alpha-subunit with a helical structure similar to type 1 cytokines like IL-6 and a beta-subunit structurally related to the extracellular regions of Type 1 cytokine receptors (e.g. soluble IL-6 receptor). The alpha subunits are encoded by IL12A, IL23A and IL27A while the beta subunits are encoded by IL12B and EBI3 and co-expression of both chains is required for secretion of the bioactive cytokine.

nodes.name: Calcyphosine family
nodes.description: The Calcyphosines encode a distinct family of calcium binding EF hand domain proteins.

nodes.name: Docking protein family
nodes.description: The mammalian Dok protein family has seven members(DOK1–DOK7). The DOK proteins share structural similarities characterized by the NH 2-terminal pleckstrin homology and phosphotyrosine-binding domains followed by SH2 target motifs in the COOH-terminalmoiety, indicating an adapter function.

nodes.name: SM family of SNARE chaperones
nodes.description: SM proteins interact with SNAREs and, like SNAREs, are essential for membrane fusion in vivo. Each SM protein interacts with one or more distinct sets of client SNAREs. X-ray structures of SM proteins have now been reported, and they are all very similar, the most notable feature being a large cleft created by a helical hairpin in domain 3a that extends, somewhat like a thumb, away from the globular body of the protein. There is strong support for the idea that SM proteins function as chaperones, their essential role being to enable fast, accurate SNARE assembly.

nodes.name: JOSD family MJD deubiquinating enzymes
nodes.description: The four members of the MJD deubiquinating enzymes fall into two subfamilies based on phylogenetic analysis and domain structure - the JOSD family (JOSD1 and JOSD2) and the Ataxin 3 family. The proteins encoded by the paralogs JOSD1 and JOSD2 are much smaller than ATXN3 and ATXN3L and consist solely of a catalytic Josephin domain.

nodes.name: SERF domain containing
nodes.description: All members of this group encode a Small EDRK-rich factor-like, N-terminal domain (InterPro IPR007513).

nodes.name: Dehydrocholesterol reductases
nodes.description: In the cholesterol synthesis pathway, there are four sterol reductases that catalyze three distinct reductive steps on sterol intermediates. Three of the enzymes, 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase (DHCR7), TM7SF2 (transmembrane 7 superfamily member 2), and lamin B receptor (LBR), share evolutionary ties with a high level of sequence homology and predicted structural homology. DHCR24 (24-dehydrocholesterol reductase) is not homologous to the other three genes. TM7SF2 and LBR uniquely share the same delta-14 reductase activity in cholesterol biosynthesis. Depending on which synthesis pathway is following the terminal enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis is either DHCR7 (Kandutsch–Russell pathway) or DHCR24 (Bloch pathway).

nodes.name: EXPERA domain containing
nodes.description: The EXPERA domain is conserved among the TM6SF family (TM6SF1 and TM6SF2), TMEM97 and EBP. EBP has cholestenol delta-isomerase activity and it is likely that other EXPERA domain proteins also possess sterol isomerase activity. The EXPERA domain contains four transmembrane regions and is present twice in TM6SF proteins and once in TMEM97 and EBP.

nodes.name: Cysteine rich hydrophobic domain family
nodes.description: The CHIC family are small, palmitoylated, membrane-associated proteins, depending on the palmitoylation of cysteines in the CHIC motif for their membrane association.

nodes.name: EvC complex subunits
nodes.description: A heterotetramer EvC complex, composed of two sub-complexes (IQCE-EFCAB7 and EVC-EVC2), is a positive regulator of Hedgehog signaling pathway. EFCAB7 binds to the C-terminal region of EVC2 and N-terminus of IQCE thus acting as a critical link between IQCE and the EVC-EVC2 complex.The EFCAB7-IQCE module anchors the EVC-EVC2 complex in a signaling microdomain at the base of cilia.

nodes.name: TP53 regulating kinase family
nodes.description: TP53RK (TP53 regulating kinase) also known as PRPK (p53-related protein kinase) is the human homologue of yeast Bud32. TP53RK phosphorylates TP53 at Ser15. Activation of TP53RK kinase activity is mediated by another kinase, AKT1, which phosphorylates TP53RK at Ser250.

nodes.name: Histone H3 associated protein kinase family
nodes.description: HASPIN (histone H3 associated protein kinase haploid) is an atypical serine/threonine-protein kinase that was for a long time considered an inactive pseudokinase due to low degree of structural homology of HASPIN with the 'classical' protein kinases. However, the discovery of HASPIN-catalyzed phosphorylation of histone H3 at Thr3 residue unveiled importance of HASPIN in mitosis and provided yet another link between mitotic phosphorylation pathways and chromatin modifications.

nodes.name: MOS proto-oncogene, serine/threonine kinase family
nodes.description: The MOS proto-oncogene-encoded serine/threonine protein kinase plays a key cell cycle-regulatory role during meiosis.

nodes.name: PTEN induced kinase 1 family
nodes.description: PINK1 is one of the most divergent human protein kinases. It contains an N-terminal mitochondria-targeting and transmembrane segment, an unconserved region, a kinase domain with three insertions in the N lobe, and a conserved C-terminal region (CTR) of unknown function and structure. Although distinct from other kinases, PINK1 is highly conserved across species. PINK1 phosphorylates both ubiquitin and the ubiquitin-like domain of PRKN (parkin RBR E3 ubiquitin protein ligase) on structurally protected Ser65 residues, triggering the mitochondrial quality-control process mitophagy. Mutations in PINK1 can cause the neurodegenerative condition Parkinson disease (PD).

nodes.name: Cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor 1 family
nodes.description: The CDKN1 family (CIP/KIP family) encompassing CDKN1A (p21CIP), CDKN1B (p27KIP1) and CDKN1C (p57KIP2) are able to bind all the major cell cycle promoting Cyclin/CDK complexes (Cyclin A, B, D, E with respective CDK1,2,4,6), and depending on their posttranslational modification, they can either inhibit or promote the activity of bound Cyclin/CDK complexes.

nodes.name: Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor families
nodes.description: Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitors are small nucleocytoplasmic proteins belonging to two families– the CDKN1 family (CIP/KIP family) encompassing CDKN1A (p21CIP), CDKN1B (p27KIP1) and CDKN1C (p57KIP2), and the CDKN2 family (INK4 family) encompassing CDKN2A (p16INK4a), CDKN2B (p15INK4b), CDKN2C (p18INK4c) and CDKN2DA (p19INK4d). CDKN1 family members are able to bind all the major cell cycle promoting Cyclin/CDK complexes (Cyclin A, B, D, E with respective CDK1,2,4,6), and depending on their posttranslational modification, they can either inhibit or promote the activity of bound Cyclin/CDK complexes. On the other hand, CDKN2 family members can bind only to Cyclin D/CDK4/6 complexes and work as inhibitors. In non-transformed cells, members of both families usually collaborate to regulate development, differentiation, and stem cell pool and have partially overlapping functions. However, in transformed cells, almost all the members are gaining new tumor-enhancing functions such as increasing survival, stimulating DNA repair, and apoptosis resistance

nodes.name: Cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor 2 family
nodes.description: The CDKN2 family (INK4 family) encompassing CDKN2A (p16INK4a), CDKN2B (p15INK4b), CDKN2C (p18INK4c) and CDKN2DA (p19INK4d) can bind only to Cyclin D/CDK4/6 complexes and work as inhibitors.

nodes.name: Mitogen-activated protein kinase 7 (ERK5) family
nodes.description: MAPK7(ERK5) is the sole member of one of four subfamilies of conventional MAPKs. Activation of each group of conventional MAPKs depends on a set of two upstream, evolutionarily conserved, sequentially acting kinases. MAPK7 is activated by different extracellular stimuli, including growth factors, inflammatory cytokines, oxidative and osmotic stresses, ischaemia, and hypoxia. The MAP3Ks activated by these extracellular stimuli are MAP3K2 (MEKK2) and MAP3K3 (MEKK3), which specifically phosphorylate the MAP2K MAP2K5 (MEK5), which in turn, directly activates MAPK7 through phosphorylation of both tyrosine and threonine residues of the Thr-Glu-Tyr motif present within the activation loop of the MAPK7 kinase domain. Because of its unique extended C-terminus containing a nuclear localization signal, two proline-rich regions, and a transcriptional activation domain, it appears that the most significant role of MAPK7 is to regulate a number of downstream transcription factors.

nodes.name: Aconitases
nodes.description: Two aconitase (EC 4.2.1.3) isoforms are present in mammalian cells: the mitochondrial aconitase (ACO2) that catalyzes the reversible isomerization of citrate to isocitrate in the citric acid cycle, and the bifunctional cytosolic enzyme (ACO1), which also plays a role as an RNA-binding protein in the regulation of intracellular iron metabolism. Aconitase activities in the different subcellular compartments can be selectively inactivated by different genetic defects, iron depletion, and oxidative or nitrative stress. Aconitase contains a [4Fe-4S]2+ cluster that is essential for substrate coordination and catalysis.

nodes.name: Carbon-oxygen lyases
nodes.description: These genes encode enzymes with carbon-oxygen lyase activities (EC 4.2.-.-).

nodes.name: Hydroperoxy icosatetraenoate dehydratases
nodes.description: The genes in this group encode enzymes with hydroperoxy icosatetraenoate dehydratase activity (EC 4.2.1.152).

nodes.name: Carbon-nitrogen lyases
nodes.description: These genes encode enzymes with carbon-nitrogen lyase activities (EC 4.3.-.-).

nodes.name: DNA-(apurinic or apyrimidinic site) lyases
nodes.description: These genes encode enzymes with DNA-(apurinic or apyrimidinic site) lyase activity (EC 4.2.99.18).

nodes.name: CSF1R, KIT, FLT3 receptor tyrosine kinase family
nodes.description: KIT, FMS and FLT3 are considered a distinct subgroup from PDGFRA and PDGFRB in class III RTKs because they bind ligands of the four-helix bundle fold instead of the PDGF-like cystine-knot fold.

nodes.name: ALK and LTK ligand family
nodes.description: ALKAL1 and ALKAL2 are ligands that activate the receptor tyrosine kinases ALK and LTK.

nodes.name: KIND domain containing
nodes.description: The kinase non-catalytic c-lobe domain (KIND) evolved from the catalytic protein kinase fold into a potential protein interaction module for signalling proteins.

nodes.name: HtrA serine protease family
nodes.description: The HtrA family of proteins consists of evolutionarily conserved ATP-independent serine proteases which are homologs of the heat shock-induced HtrA/DegP (High temperature requirement A/Degradation of extracellular proteins) protease from the bacterium Escherichia coli. They are well conserved in evolution and widely expressed among prokaryotic and eukaryotic organisms from bacteria to mammals, including humans. General function of these proteases is to control quality of cellular proteins. HtrA proteases recognize aberrant proteins presenting exposed hydrophobic stretches and degrade them. In this way they reduce the amount of unfolded, misfolded or otherwise damaged proteins arising in a cell as the result of improper folding or action of stress-inducing agents.

nodes.name: U2AF homology motif kinase family
nodes.description: The U2AF Homology Motif Kinase 1 (UHMK1) is the only kinase that contains the U2AF homology motif, a common protein interaction domain among splicing factors. Through this motif, UHMK1 interacts with the splicing factors SF1 and SF3B1, known to participate in the 3' splice site recognition during the early steps of spliceosome assembly.

nodes.name: DSTYK family
nodes.description: DSTYK (also known as Dusty), a single-copy gene that arose in metazoan evolution and encodes a putative dual Ser/Thr and Tyr protein kinase with unique structural features. DSTYK is widely expressed in vertebrates, broadly distributed in the central nervous system, and deregulated in certain human cancers. DSTYK/Dusty proteins from lower to higher species display an increasing degree of sequence conservation from the N-terminal non-catalytic domain to C-terminal catalytic domain. The non-catalytic region has eight conserved cysteine residues, multiple potential kinase-docking motifs and phosphorylation sites, whereas the catalytic domain is divergent and about equally distant of Ser/Thr and Tyr protein kinases. Homology analyses identified the essential catalytic residues, suggesting that DSTYK/Dusty homologues all possess the enzymatic activity of a protein kinase.

nodes.name: STK31 kinase family
nodes.description: STK31 is a putative serine/threonine kinase.

nodes.name: DNA primases
nodes.description: There are two human genes that encode DNA primase activity (EC 2.7.7.102). PRIM1 encodes the small catalytic subunit of the nuclear DNA primase complex and PRIMPOL encodes the mitochondrial DNA primase that also functions as a DNA polymerase.

nodes.name: DNA primase complex subunits
nodes.description: DNA primase synthesizes short RNA primers that are required to initiate nuclear DNA synthesis on the parental template strands during DNA replication. Eukaryotic primase contains two subunits, PRIM1 (p48) and PRIM2 (p58), and is normally tightly associated with DNA polymerase alpha.

nodes.name: Enoyl-CoA hydratases
nodes.description: This group contains genes encoding enoyl-CoA hydratase activity (EC 4.2.1.17). Two of these (HADHA and EHHADH) are multifunctional enzymes.

nodes.name: 3-hydroxyacyl-[acyl-carrier-protein] dehydratases
nodes.description: This group contains genes encoding 3-hydroxyacyl-[acyl-carrier-protein] dehydratase activity (EC 4.2.1.59). FASN is a multifunctional enzyme.

nodes.name: Pterin-4 alpha-carbinolamine dehydratases
nodes.description: This group contains genes encoding pterin-4 alpha-carbinolamine dehydratase activity (EC 4.2.1.96). The PCBD1 and PCBD2 are paralogs and the encoded enzyme share 60% amino acid identity.

nodes.name: BMP receptors
nodes.description: Bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs) bind to selective combinations of type I and type II BMP receptors (BMPRIs and BMPRIIs). BMPs are dimers and can interact with heteromeric complexes of two BMPRIIs and two BMPRIs. Whereas the type II receptor BMPR2 is selective for BMPs, the other two BMPRIIs, ACVR2A and ACVR2B, can interact with BMPs and activins. There are four BMPRIs: BMPR1A (ALK3), BMPR1B (ALK6), ACVRL1 (ALK1) and ACVR1 (ALK2). BMP2 and BMP4 bind more strongly to BMPR1A and BMPR1B, BMP6, and BMP7 bind most strongly to ACVR1, and BMP9 and BMP10 are high affinity ligands for ACVRL1 but can also bind to ACVR1. Both receptor types share high structural and sequence similarity; they are both single pass transmembrane proteins composed of extracellular domains that are rich in cysteines and intracellular regions which harbor the kinase domain.

nodes.name: Dectin 1 cluster
nodes.description: The Dectin-1 cluster is one of two genomic regions within the natural killer gene complex (NKC) on the human chromosome 12 (and the corresponding region in the mouse chromosome 6) encoding C-type lectin receptors. The Dectin-1 cluster is located in the centromeric part of the NKC, while the Dectin-2 cluster is encoded at the telomeric end of the NKC. All the receptors included in these clusters are type II transmembrane receptors, where the C-terminal encodes the extracellular region of the protein consisting of a single CTLD and a stalk domain, connected to an intracellular domain via a transmembrane region. Whereas all the receptors in the Dectin-1 cluster contain one or more functional motifs within their intracellular tails that allow them to induce intracellular signaling on its own, members of the Dectin-2 cluster (with the exception of CLEC4A) induce intracellular signaling through signaling adaptors.

nodes.name: Dectin 2 cluster
nodes.description: The Dectin-2 cluster is one of two genomic regions within the natural killer gene complex (NKC) on the human chromosome 12 (and the corresponding region in the mouse chromosome 6) encoding C-type lectin receptors. The Dectin-2 cluster is located at the telomeric end of the NKC, while the Dectin-1 cluster is encoded in the centromeric part of the NKC. All the receptors included in these clusters are type II transmembrane receptors, where the C-terminal encodes the extracellular region of the protein consisting of a single CTLD and a stalk domain, connected to an intracellular domain via a transmembrane region. Whereas all the receptors in the Dectin-1 cluster contain one or more functional motifs within their intracellular tails that allow them to induce intracellular signaling on its own, members of the Dectin-2 cluster (with the exception of CLEC4A) induce intracellular signaling through signaling adaptors.

nodes.name: Angel homologs
nodes.description: The paralogs ANGEL1 and ANGEL2 encode enzymes with 2′,3′-cyclic phosphatase activity. RNA molecules are frequently modified with a terminal 2′,3′-cyclic phosphate group as a result of endonuclease cleavage, exonuclease trimming, or de novo synthesis. During pre-transfer RNA (tRNA) and unconventional messenger RNA (mRNA) splicing, 2′,3′-cyclic phosphates are substrates of the tRNA ligase complex, and their removal is critical for recycling of tRNAs upon ribosome stalling. ANGEL1 displays a weak 2′,3′-cyclic phosphatase activity relative to ANGEL2.

nodes.name: WEE family tyrosine specific kinases
nodes.description: WEE1 and WEE2 are closely related members of the WEE family of protein kinases, sharing over 40% amino acid identity. Both WEE1 and WEE2 are tyrosine specific kinases that inhibit CDK1 through phosphorylation of Tyr15. WEE1 prevents entry into mitosis at the G2-M transition. WEE2 expression is germ-cell-specific and inhibits meiosis. In contrast the third, more diverged member of the family, PKMYT1 is a dual specificity protein kinase that inhibits CDK1 by phosphorylating Thr14 and Tyr15.

nodes.name: WEE family dual specificity kinases
nodes.description: PKMYT1 shares structural similarities with other members of the WEE kinase family, featuring an N-lobe and C-lobe connected through a hinge region. Functionally, both WEE1 and PKMYT1 phosphorylate CDK1, a master regulator of mitotic entry, to inhibit its activity and prevent its interaction with cyclin B. However, PKMYT1 is distinct from WEE1 in that it phosphorylates CDK1 at both Thr14 and Tyr15 residues, while WEE1 solely phosphorylates CDK1 at Tyr15.

nodes.name: Popeye domain cAMP effector family
nodes.description: The Popeye domain-containing (POPDC) gene family, consisting of POPDC1 (also known as BVES), POPDC2, and POPDC3, encodes transmembrane proteins abundantly expressed in striated muscle. POPDC proteins are cAMP effector proteins and have been proposed to be part of the protein network involved in cAMP signaling.

nodes.name: Phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase type 3 family
nodes.description: There are four mammalian phosphatidylinositol 4-kinases (PI4Ks), composed of Types II and III, which generate PI4P from PI. The Type III PI4Ks are composed of two isoforms, PI4KA PI4KB. Both PI4KA and PI4KB are peripheral membrane-binding proteins, while the Type II PI4Ks are lipidated with their membrane localization being regulated both by lipidation and post-translational modifications. The targeted recruitment and activation of PI4KA and PI4KB on membranes is critical to their regulation. PI4P generated by PI4KA and PI4KB plays essential roles at the Golgi/trans-Golgi network (TGN) and plasma membrane (PM) leading to membrane recruitment of proteins, modulation of integral membrane protein activity and lipid transport between organelles. Type III PI4Ks are structurally homologous to the PI3Ks.

nodes.name: Nucleoside/nucleotide kinases
nodes.description: This group contains genes that encode kinases that act on nucleoside or nucleotide substrates.

nodes.name: Inositol-trisphosphate 3-kinase family
nodes.description: Inositol-trisphosphate [Ins(1,4,5)P 3] 3-kinases (ITPKs) phosphorylate the intracellular second messenger Ins(1,4,5)P 3. These enzymes terminate the signal to release Ca2+ from the endoplasmic reticulum and produce the messenger inositol tetrakisphosphate [Ins(1,3,4,5)P 4]. Independent of their enzymatic activity, ITPKs regulate the microstructure of the actin cytoskeleton.

nodes.name: Inositol hexakisphosphate kinase family
nodes.description: Inositol is a unique biological small molecule that can be phosphorylated or even further pyrophosphorylated on each of its six hydroxyl groups. These numerous phosphorylation states of inositol along with the kinases and phosphatases that interconvert them comprise the inositol phosphate signaling pathway. Inositol hexakisphosphate kinases, or IP6Ks, convert the fully mono-phosphorylated inositol to the pyrophosphate 5-IP7 (also denoted IP7). There are three isoforms of IP6K: IP6K1, IP6K2, and IP6K3.

nodes.name: Cytidine/uridine monophosphate kinases
